# Week 3

## 2026/10/05

Given that the Julia script was written by somebody else, it was difficult to debug. It was therefore decided that it would be more efficient to rewrite the script in `bash` The script goes to the point of plotting the lightcurves for all three instruments.

The script was added to the shared GitHub repository to download onto solva for testing. A useful command to remember to download a single file from GitHub is:

```{.bash .code-overflow-wrap}
wget --no-check-certificate --content-disposition https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phajy/project-iron-lines/main/code/XMM-Pipeline.sh
```

It is clear that the Julia script does not compute a step, or does not do so correctly and thus in further analysis the bash script will be used.

## 2026/10/09

### Reprocessing the 0693781301 Dataset Using the PN Instrument

Given the recommendation to use data from the PN instrument, the data was reprocessed. First the bash script was ran with the command

```{.bash}
/data/cluster4/BradleyAndJacob/Scripts/XMM-Pipeline.sh
```

The resulting lightcurve is shown below

![The pn lightcurve of the observation. A large flare is again observed at the end of the observation, which was filtered out from the data analysis.](images/pn_ltcrv.png)

There is once again a flare towards the end so the GTI was set such that RATE is always less than 30

```{.bash}
# Setting Environment Variables
export SAS_ODFPATH="$(pwd)"
export SAS_CCFPATH="/opt/local/XMM/ccf/"
export SAS_CCF="$SAS_ODFPATH/ccf.cif"
export SAS_ODF="$SAS_ODFPATH/$(ls *SUM.SAS)"

# Creating the GTI (Good Time Interval) file for time filtering
tabgtigen table=pn_ltcrv.fits gtiset=gtiset.fits expression='RATE<=30' 

# Filtering the events file using the GTI
evselect table=pn_filt.fits filtertype=expression filteredset=pn_filt_time.fits expression='GTI(gtiset.fits,TIME)' 

# Creating an attitude file
atthkgen atthkset=attitude.fits

# Creating an image for soft X-ray detections
evselect table=pn_filt_time.fits withimageset=yes imageset=pn-s.fits imagebinning=binSize xcolumn=X ximagebinsize=82 ycolumn=Y yimagebinsize=82 filtertype=expression expression='(FLAG == 0)&&(PI in [300:2000])'

# Creating an image for hard X-ray detections
evselect table=pn_filt_time.fits withimageset=yes imageset=pn-h.fits imagebinning=binSize xcolumn=X ximagebinsize=82 ycolumn=Y yimagebinsize=82 filtertype=expression expression='(FLAG == 0)&&(PI in [2000:10000])'

# Creating an image for all X-ray detections
evselect table=pn_filt_time.fits withimageset=yes imageset=pn-all.fits imagebinning=binSize xcolumn=X ximagebinsize=82 ycolumn=Y yimagebinsize=82 filtertype=expression expression='(FLAG == 0)&&(PI in [300:10000])'
```

The regions selected for source and background extraction were centred on (25628, 23912). The source region was a circle with radius 1000 pixels, and the background was an annulus with inner/outer radii 2000/4000 pixels, respectively.

![The regions selected for source and background extraction. The scale at the bottom denotes how many events were detected in each pixel.](images/0693781301_regions.png)

```{.bash}
eexpmap imageset=pn-h.fits attitudeset=attitude.fits eventset=pn_filt_time.fits expimageset=pn_expmap_2-10keV.fits pimin=2000 pimax=10000

# Extract the Source Spectrum
evselect table='pn_filt_time.fits' energycolumn='PI' filteredset='pn_filtered.fits' filtertype='expression' expression='((X,Y) in CIRCLE(25628,23912,1000))' spectrumset='pn_pi.fits' spectralbinsize=5 withspecranges=yes specchannelmin=0 specchannelmax=20479

# Extract the Background Spectrum
evselect table=pn_filt_time.fits energycolumn='PI' filteredset='bkg_filtered.fits' filtertype='expression' spectrumset='bkg_pi.fits' spectralbinsize=5 expression='((X,Y) in CIRCLE(25628,23912,4000))&&!((X,Y) in CIRCLE(25628,23912,2000))' withspecranges=yes specchannelmin=0 specchannelmax=20479

# Check for Pileup
epatplot set=pn_filtered.fits plotfile=pn_epat.ps useplotfile=yes withbackgroundset=yes backgroundset=bkg_filtered.fits

# Find the source and background region areas for the ancillary file
backscale spectrumset=pn_pi.fits badpixlocation=pn_filt_time.fits
backscale spectrumset=bkg_pi.fits badpixlocation=pn_filt_time.fits

# Generate the Photon Redistribution Matrix
rmfgen rmfset=pn_rmf.fits spectrumset=pn_pi.fits 

# Generate the Ancillary File
arfgen arfset=pn_arf.fits spectrumset=pn_pi.fits withrmfset=yes rmfset=pn_rmf.fits withbadpixcorr=yes badpixlocation=pn_filt_time.fits 
```

The files were then moved to a products folder with

```{.bash}
# Making a folder for the products
mkdir ../PRODUCTS

# Storing the observation ID as a variable
export OBSID="0693781301"

# Moving and renaming the product files
cp pn_pi.fits ../PRODUCTS/$(echo $OBSID)_pn_pi.fits
cp bkg_pi.fits ../PRODUCTS/$(echo $OBSID)_pn_bkg_pi.fits
cp pn_rmf.fits ../PRODUCTS/$(echo $OBSID)_pn_rmf.fits
cp pn_arf.fits ../PRODUCTS/$(echo $OBSID)_pn_arf.fits
```

The products could then be plotted, which was once again done with Julia. Per our supervisor's suggestion, the data was rebinned which was completed using the tool `ftgrouppha` as follows:

```{.bash}
ftgrouppha 0693781301_pn_pi.fits 0693781301_pn_pi_rebin.fits grouptype=min groupscale=400
ftgrouppha 0693781301_pn_bkg_pi.fits 0693781301_pn_bkg_pi_rebin.fits grouptype=min groupscale=400
```

The resulting spectrum is plotted below

![The pn spectrum of MCG-6-30-15 from observation ID 0693781301, regrouped to have at least 400 counts per bin. The red line marks 6.4 keV where the Fe K$\alpha$ emission line is expected. A bump is observed in the expected region.](images/0693781301_pn_spectrum.png)

The next steps are to fit a power law continuum and observe the ratio between the data and the model. This will be done through the XSPEC software, it will be necessary to mask the region around the iron line such that it doesn't interfere with the fit. Similarly, the soft X-ray region below ~2.5 keV will need to be masked.

The response and background files can be linked to the spectrum file, and the rebinning completed using the `ftools` utility `grppha` as follows:

```{.bash}
grppha 
mos1_pi.fits                    # input spectrum filename
mos1_grp30.fits                 # output spectrum filename
chkey BACKFILE bkg_pi.fits      # include background spectrum
chkey RESPFILE mos1_rmf.fits    # include the RMF
chkey ANCRFILE mos1_arf.fits    # include the ARF
group min 300                   # group the data by 300 counts/bin
exit
```

## 2026/10/10

### A Julia Script for Spectrum Plotting

In order to quickly view the produced spectra, a julia script was produced as shown below. Note that some formatting lines have been excluded for brevity, the full code can be found on the [Project GitHub Repository](https://github.com/phajy/project-iron-lines/tree/main/code). The code makes use of the `SpectralFitting.jl` library @baker_spectralfittingjl_2025.

:::{.callout-note collapse="true" title="ViewSpectrum.jl Source Code"}
```{.julia}
using SpectralFitting, Plots, LaTeXStrings, ArgParse

# Data loading function
function LoadData(
    spectrum::String; 
    dataRange::Tuple{Real, Real}=(2,10)
    )

    # Loading in the spectrum file
    data = OGIPDataset(spectrum)

    # Regrouping, normalising, dropping bad channels and curtailing
    regroup!(data)
    normalize!(data)
    drop_bad_channels!(data)
    mask_energies!(data, dataRange...)
end

function ParseArguments()
    s = ArgParseSettings()

    #Add arguments with their default values
    @add_arg_table s begin
        "--OBS_ID"
            help="The observation ID"
            default="MISSING"
        "--Instrument"
            help="XMM EPIC Instrument name (pn, mos1, mos2)"
            default="pn"
        "--INDIR"
            help="The input directory"
            default=pwd()
        "--OUTDIR"
            help="The output directory"
            default=pwd()
    end

    return parse_args(ARGS, s)
end

args = ParseArguments()

# Loading the data (requires that the spectrum files are grouped)
data = LoadData(
    "$(args["INDIR"])/$(args["OBS_ID"])_$(args["Instrument"])_pi_rebinned.fits"
)

# Setting the observation id
data.user_data.observation_id = args["OBS_ID"]

# Plotting
majorticks = collect(2:10)
vline([6.4]; c=:red, ls=:dash, lw=0.7, label=L"Fe K$\alpha$")
plt = plot!(
    data; ylabel=L"Counts (s$^{-1}$ keV$^{-1}$)", 
    xaxis=:log, yaxis=:log, xticks=(majorticks, majorticks),
    c=:black, markercolor=:black, lc=:black, lw=0.5, msw=0.,
    framestyle=:box, xlims=(minimum(majorticks), maximum(majorticks))
)

# Saving the figure
savefig(
    plt, "$(args["OUTDIR"])/$(args["OBS_ID"])_$(args["Instrument"])_spectrum.png"
)
```
:::

To call the script, the following is used

```{.bash}
julia PATH_TO_SCRIPT/ViewSpectrum.jl --OBS_ID --Instrument --INDIR --OUTDIR
```

The code currently assumes that the spectrum file follows the convention `[OBS_ID]_[Instrument]_pi.fits` (where `[Instrument]` can be `pn`, `mos1` or `mos2`) and that the spectrum file points to the background and response files (which can be accomplished either with `grppha`, or `specgroup`). The `specgroup` usage follows the syntax 

```{.bash}
specgroup spectrumset=srcspec.ds addfilenames=yes arfset=myarf.ds rmfset=myrmf.ds backgndset=mybgnd.ds
```

## Summary of Data Reduction Commands

Two more bash scripts were made for an intermediate step (`Image-Pipeline.sh`) and the final steps (`Final-Pipeline.sh`) respectively. With these, the data reduction only requires the following commands to be run:

### Reprocessing

```{.bash}
# Run the initial pipeline script
bash /data/cluster4/BradleyAndJacob/Scripts/XMM-Pipeline.sh

# Setting Environment Variables
export SAS_ODFPATH="$(pwd)"
export SAS_CCFPATH="/opt/local/XMM/ccf/"
export SAS_CCF="$SAS_ODFPATH/ccf.cif"
export SAS_ODF="$SAS_ODFPATH/$(ls *SUM.SAS)"
export INSTRUMENT="pn"

# Enter the processing directory
cd ../PROC
```

### GTI Filtering

After viewing the lightcurve and determining a filtering expression for a GTI, run

```{.bash}
# Creating the GTI (Good Time Interval) file for time filtering
tabgtigen table="$INSTRUMENT"_ltcrv.fits gtiset=gtiset.fits expression='RATE<=30' 

# Run the image generation pipeline
bash /data/cluster4/BradleyAndJacob/Scripts/Image-Pipeline.sh $INSTRUMENT
```

### Region Selection

Then, open the image in ds9 and select the source and background regions

```{.bash}
# View the image and select regions
ds9 $INSTRUMENT-all.fits &

# Set region expressions as variables, replacing X, Y and R
export SOURCE_CENTRE="X,Y"
export SOURCE_REGION=""$SOURCE_CENTRE",R"
export BACKGROUND_REGION_INNER=""$SOURCE_CENTRE",R"
export BACKGROUND_REGION_OUTER=""$SOURCE_CENTRE",R"
```

### Spectrum Extraction

Then enter one of the following pairs of commands, for the relevant instrument

```{.bash}
# ========== For PN ========== 
# Extract the Source Spectrum
evselect table="$INSTRUMENT"_filt_time.fits energycolumn="PI" filteredset="$INSTRUMENT"_filtered.fits filtertype="expression" expression="((X,Y) in CIRCLE("$SOURCE_REGION"))&&(FLAG==0)&&(PATTERN<=4)" spectrumset=""$INSTRUMENT"_pi.fits" spectralbinsize=5 withspecranges=yes specchannelmin=0 specchannelmax=20479

# Extract the Background Spectrum
evselect table="$INSTRUMENT"_filt_time.fits energycolumn="PI" filteredset="bkg_filtered.fits" filtertype="expression" spectrumset="bkg_pi.fits" spectralbinsize=5 expression="((X,Y) in CIRCLE("$BACKGROUND_REGION_OUTER"))&&!((X,Y) in CIRCLE("$BACKGROUND_REGION_INNER"))&&(FLAG==0)&&(PATTERN<=4)" withspecranges=yes specchannelmin=0 specchannelmax=20479
# ========== For PN ========== 

# ========= For MOS  ========= 
# Extract the Source Spectrum
evselect table="$INSTRUMENT"_filt_time.fits energycolumn="PI" filteredset=""$INSTRUMENT"_filtered.fits" filtertype="expression" expression="((X,Y) in CIRCLE("$SOURCE_REGION"))" spectrumset=""$INSTRUMENT"_pi.fits" spectralbinsize=5 withspecranges=yes specchannelmin=0 specchannelmax=11999

# Extract the Background Spectrum
evselect table="$INSTRUMENT"_filt_time.fits energycolumn="PI" filteredset="bkg_filtered.fits" filtertype="expression" spectrumset="bkg_pi.fits" spectralbinsize=5 expression="((X,Y) in CIRCLE("$BACKGROUND_REGION_OUTER"))&&!((X,Y) in CIRCLE("$BACKGROUND_REGION_INNER"))" withspecranges=yes specchannelmin=0 specchannelmax=11999
# ========= For MOS  ========= 
```

### Pileup Check

Check the spectrum for pileup

```{.bash}
# Check for Pileup
epatplot set="$INSTRUMENT"_filtered.fits plotfile="$INSTRUMENT"_epat.ps useplotfile=yes withbackgroundset=yes backgroundset=bkg_filtered.fits
```

### Response Files and Cleanup

If there is no pileup, run the final script, otherwise reselect the source region to exclude the centre and reduce pileup

```{.bash}
# If no pileup, run the final pipeline
bash /data/cluster4/BradleyAndJacob/Scripts/Final-Pipeline.sh [OBS_ID] $INSTRUMENT 
```

### Test Data

This pipeline was tested on the MCG-6-30-15 dataset with observation ID 0111570101. The GTI was set with the expression "TIME>=79698000", abd the regions were centred at (26880,27661) with radii 1000,2000,4000. The resulting spectrum from the pn instrument (after grouping the bins in groups of 4, cutting the data to 1024 channels) is shown below.

![The spectrum from obsid 0111570101. The data was once again plotted with ViewSpectrum.jl](images/0111570101_pn_spectrum.png)

This showed a successful spectrum extraction, and yet another promising dataset. The next steps are to thus begin fitting to data in order to reproduce a plot similar to Figure 1 in Fabian et al. (2002) @fabian_long_2002.
